houseBegin.say: You have seen the houses. Each keeps an Art, and each will ask.
Hear all three before you choose. A pledge is not lightly made.

houseStorm.say: Arlo Kestrel. We keep the Storm, and the Storm keeps nobody waiting.
Pledge here and you climb before you walk. Lightning likes the heights.

houseLamp.say: We mend what the sea breaks, and we keep the lamps lit.
Pledge with us and you will walk the Moors, where ships are lost.

houseVeil.say: Sable. That is all the name you will get.
We read what the Tithe writes. Pledge here and you read it too.

stormBegin.say: The Tithe took our storm-glass from the Old Beacon. Pell went after it.
Climb to the beacon. I will speak to you on the wind.

stormBeacon.say: Empty racks. Tithe boot prints. They carried it down to their camp.
Pell's knife is in the grass. He was here, and not alone.

stormCamp.say: Take back what they carried. And gather Brineglass. It holds a storm.

stormGlass.say: That is our glass. Now climb as high as you can.

stormCalled.say: Hold the glass up. Let the storm find you. There.
The Storm is yours now, and it will answer when you call.

stormTrail.say: Pell was seen at Weir Mill. Call the storm as you go.

stormMill.say: Pell took the river road with Tithe riders. You will need quicker feet.
Let the storm into your legs. We call it Quicken.

stormRiders.say: The riders carry the tally to the meadows. Run them down.

stormLedger.say: The tally names a ship. Our glass is going to sea.

stormSea.say: Take a ship out. Find a Tithe sail and beat it.

stormIsle.say: Their crew talked. The glass went ashore on an isle they guard.

stormRods.say: Lightning rods, wrapped in Tithe cloth. They meant to keep the storm themselves.
Take one. Shape the storm as you like it.

stormPoint.say: Someone lit Grey Point Light with lightning last night. Only a Stormcaller can.

stormPell.say: I lit it for them. They said it would pay my family's tenth.
Corvane is counting the storm. He means to sell it back to us.
Come home, Pell. And you, take this. We call it Arc Lash.

stormMaw.say: The High Assessor waits in the Maw. End his counting.

stormCorvane.say: Everything is owed. Even the storm.

stormHome.say: The racks are full again. Pell is mending them himself.
You climbed before you walked. That is a Stormcaller.
Thank you. I will not sell the sky again.

lampBegin.say: False lights burn on the Driftwood Moors. Ships follow them onto the rocks.
Go to the wrecks. Our lamps will let me speak to you there.

lampHulks.say: Are you real? The light was right there. Then the rocks.
That boy lived. Keep him safe, and find who lit that light.

lampGraves.say: The false lights burn by the graves. Put them out, and gather Brineglass.

lampDoused.say: Pirates. They were waiting for us to break.
Bring him to Moorend. He should not walk the moor alone.

lampSunwell.say: You kept him safe. That is the whole of what we do.
Stand still, and let the light rise round you. That is the Sunwell.

lampHamlet.say: Saltgrass took in the other wrecked. Raise the light there, and see them.

lampSaltgrass.say: The hamlet says the Tithe came for the dead as well.
Then we mend the living first. Your hands know how now.

lampBarrows.say: Tithe collectors are opening the barrows. Stop them, and mend whoever bleeds.

lampCoin.say: Pirate silver in Tithe purses. Someone pays the wreckers.
Find their ship. It will be near the coast, waiting for the next.

lampSea.say: Take a ship out. Find the wreckers' sail and stop it.

lampCove.say: Their captain spoke of a cove. Whatever they took is buried there.

lampLens.say: That lens is ours. It was lit on the Beacon before you were born.
Choose what the light becomes in your hands.

lampStones.say: The buyer meets the Tithe at the Old Stones. Go and see who.

lampBuyer.say: Lamplighters. The Tithe bought your lens fair.
Nothing stolen is bought fair. Burn their dark away. That is Dawnflare.

lampTomb.say: The Reeve who paid them hides in the Pearl Tomb. Go.

lampReeve.say: The Tithe will light its own lamps.
Then they will burn without us. Come home.

lampHome.say: The lens is back on the Beacon. Every ship tonight will see it.
I watched it light from the quay. I knew it was yours.
You light the way now, as we do.

veilBegin.say: The Tithe wrote your name before you washed ashore. We want the page.
Go to the Hollow in the Vale. A whisper will find you there.

veilHollow.say: You are the one Thule could not drown. The Tithe still counts you.
Wren will show you the collectors. Take their tallies. They will not give them.

veilFarm.say: The collectors rest at Orchard Farm. Their tallies are on their belts.

veilTallies.say: Every tally has your name in it. And a sum.
Wait under Valeguard after dark. I will meet you there.

veilRaven.say: You walked here unseen. Good. Now let the dark take wing.
The raven is yours. It hunts what you mark.

veilChalk.say: The tallies go to the chalk pits on the Downs. Send the raven ahead.

veilRuin.say: Guards in the Adit. Too many to walk past.
Then do not walk. Throw. We call them Dusk Daggers.

veilAdit.say: Empty the Chalk Adit. Leave nothing that can count.

veilShip.say: The book went out this morning, on a Tithe ship.

veilSea.say: Find a Tithe ship and take its deck. The book will be aboard.

veilIsle.say: Only a page was aboard. The reckoner keeps the rest on an isle.

veilPage.say: Your page. Read the sum if you like.
Then choose what the dark becomes in your hands.

veilMoorhold.say: A Reeve on the Moors holds the book now. Moorhold.

veilPaid.say: Half your debt is paid already. Someone in Overlook paid it.
Interesting. Leave him. You will want to vanish now. Like this.

veilGrotto.say: The book itself is in Kraken's Grotto. Its keeper never leaves.

veilBook.say: The book. Your name. The sum. And a mark beside it, paid.

veilHome.say: I burned your page. The Tithe will have to remember you unwritten.
Who paid half? A question for another night.
We never say welcome. You will know it anyway.
